subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: For macOS app-backed nodes, should OpenClaw preserve advertised `system.which`/`system.run` and make remote skill-bin probing readiness-aware, or should it skip probes for co-located app nodes?
rationale: The choice changes remote exec compatibility, startup noise, stale-bin behavior, and skill availability freshness; current source supports the remaining risk but does not settle the intended product contract.

options.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
options.body: Preserve the macOS app command surface, delay the initial probe until node readiness is credible, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live co-located plus remote macOS proof.

options.title: Skip Co-Located App Probes Only
options.body: Suppress the same-host warning path while leaving remote macOS app probe timing to a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Disable App-node Probing By Default
options.body: Stop automatic app-node remote skill eligibility unless users explicitly enable it, reducing warnings at the cost of default remote skill support.

recommendation.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
recommendation.body: Preserve the macOS app command surface, delay the initial probe until node readiness is credible, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live co-located plus remote macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans remote skills, macOS node exec, and security/product boundaries where the strongest feature-history signal is steipete.
